conventions.convention: Eigenphases satisfy Uψ = exp(2πiθ)ψ with θ ∈ [0,1); m ≥ 1 and Q = 2^m. The phase register is big-endian, with weight 2^j on wire q_(m−1−j).
Controlled-power access and repeated single controlled-U access are distinct capabilities. Controlled inverse powers require a separate promise; forward QPE does not use U inverse.
Forward QPE applies controlled positive powers followed by the inverse of the positive-sign QFT, including its declared wire swaps.
For x ∈ [−1,1], d_T(x) = min(|x|,1−|x|). Phase error is circular distance, including wrap-around; it is not ordinary absolute error.
Readout uses the specified computational-basis Lüders branch Z ↦ P_y Z P_y. Conditional states are assigned only to positive-probability outcomes.

The gate count uses ideal exact continuous rotations, counts named SWAPs as one gate, excludes eigenstate preparation and final measurement, and asserts no fixed-alphabet compilation or uniform-family bound.
The nearest-grid bound holds for every minimizing label, including either tied label. The tail event uses ≥ η and requires K = floor(Qη) ≥ 2.

load_bearing.statement: Let m ≥ 1, Q = 2^m, and let the input be an eigenvector with Uψ = exp(2πiθ)ψ, where θ ∈ [0,1). For each y ∈ {0,…,Q−1}, the probability is P_θ(y) = Q^−2 |Σ_(j=0)^(Q−1) exp(2πij(θ−y/Q))|², including grid phases.

For the promised eigenphase input and declared forward access, initialize the registers, apply phase-register Hadamards, controlled U^(2^j) on the weight-2^j wires, the inverse positive-sign binary QFT, and the specified computational-basis Lüders readout; output y and y/Q.

For n ∈ N and z ∈ C, S_n(z) = Σ_(j=0)^(n−1) z^j equals the canonical natural n when z = 1 and (1−z^n)/(1−z) otherwise, with S_0(z) = 0. For z = exp(2πi(θ−y/Q)), z^Q = exp(2πiQθ), and z = 1 exactly when Qθ−y ∈ QZ.
For 0 ≤ u ≤ 1/2 and v ≥ 0, sin(πu) ≥ 2u and sin(v) ≤ v.

For a unitary U on nonzero finite-dimensional H, group distinct eigenphases θ into their full spectral projections Π_θ. With a_y(θ) = Q^−1 Σ_(j=0)^(Q−1) exp(2πij(θ−y/Q)) and K_y = Σ_θ a_y(θ)Π_θ, the branch is K_yψ, its probability is Σ_θ |a_y(θ)|² ||Π_θψ||², and the reference-preserving instrument is ρ ↦ (K_y ⊗ I)ρ(K_y† ⊗ I). Conditioning requires positive probability. Grid phases give spectral-projection branches; an off-grid eigenphase makes the effects nonprojective.

For m ≥ 1, Q = 2^m and θ ∈ [0,1), every nearest grid label has probability at least 4/π². If K = floor(Qη) ≥ 2, the probability of circular error at least η is at most 1/[2(K−1)]. If Qθ is an integer t, label t has probability one and all other labels have probability zero.

One run uses exactly m supplied controlled-power queries, or exactly Q−1 repeated controlled-U queries. With controlled-power circuit gate counts C_j, its unitary gate count after the eigenstate input is provided is Σ_j C_j + 2m + m(m−1)/2 + floor(m/2), in the stated ideal continuous-rotation model.

concerns.concern: Instruction 4 invokes the inverse of the exact binary QFT circuit, but deps omits alg-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit. It lists thm-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit-correct, which supplies that procedure transitively, so the mathematics remains supported. The explicit algorithm-composition rule nevertheless requires the smaller procedure's ID in the larger algorithm's deps.

seams_checked.note: QPE expressly disclaims a uniform-family or finite-alphabet bound. Its separate resource accounting does not imply either.
Positive-sign normalization, inverse negative sign, final swaps, adjoint reversal, and ideal gate counts agree. The direct procedure-dependency omission is recorded in concerns.
Big-endian weights, ordered tensor maps, tensor adjoints, and discarding the measured phase factor agree with the supplier interfaces.
Root inner products are linear first; bras and rank-one maps use the corresponding reversed Dirac pairing and coordinate matrices.
Unit vectors give trace-one rank-one densities. System and reference state spaces are nonzero where density operators are used.
Controlled access is explicitly granted; inverse access is separate. Controlled scalar phases are not discarded.
Chronological products and declared wire positions agree. Gate, query, preparation, and measurement costs remain separate.
The algorithm explicitly selects Lüders readout. The superposition theorem proves complete positivity and trace preservation and conditions only on positive-probability branches.
The orbit input is treated as an eigenphase mixture. Nearest-label recovery handles endpoint wrap-around, and repeated controlled-U cost is Q−1 per sample.

Signed Grover eigenphases, mixture weights, exact endpoint phases, and the finite kernel are preserved. The stronger two-label mass and strict tail estimate are proved locally rather than attributed to QPE.
The evaluator retains exact reflection signs, uses repeated controlled powers, converts angular error to phase error by 2π, and establishes K ≥ 20 before applying the tail bound.
Detection uses the circular tail and mixture law. Coherent reflection explicitly omits measurement, supplies inverse powers for uncomputation, and derives a vector-error bound from the kernel.

The sine-window analysis uses the geometric sum and sine bounds with their stated domains. Its different prepared window and moment estimate are derived locally; the uniform-window QPE law is not substituted.
The spectral sampler retains coherent conditional branches. Its eigenstate median guarantee checks the principal decoder and K ≥ 3, with fresh preparations and explicit access costs.

The spectral-minimum sampler establishes K ≥ 4 for its own schedule and repeats conditionally on a preserved spectral index. Power-evolution time and repeated base-unitary query costs are distinguished.
